criteria.criterion: backtest.rs D87's intervention signal uses class_of_work "code" (name and doc comments updated to say code), matching decision-sets.md section 9.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: class_of_work is now "code", the signal name ends in "class code", and the module doc's step 3 says class of work `code` and cites decision-sets.md section 9. The existing fixtures were changed from docs to code to match.

criteria.criterion: The HostError record carries a derived marker and the source intervention id. An observed record has neither, and record validation rejects a derived record without a source.
criteria.evidence: From reading records.rs: the new fields are `derived: bool` (serde default, not written when false) and `source_intervention: Option<RecordId>` (not written when None). The validation arm rejects a record when `h.derived != h.source_intervention.is_some()`. The test a_derived_host_error_needs_a_source_and_an_observed_one_has_none covers a derived record without a source, an observed record with a source, the round trip, and that an observed record writes neither field.

criteria.criterion: A derivation function takes an intervention and returns a derived HostError only when its text matches 'HTTP <code>' plus a merge operation exactly; otherwise it returns none. Unit tests cover a match, a non-match, a missing job, and an out-of-range code.
criteria.evidence: From reading watcher.rs: `derive_host_error(&Intervention) -> Option<HostError>` uses http_code (exactly 3 digits after 'HTTP ', 100 to 599) and names_merge (whole word, any case). The tests are a_refusal_stated_in_an_intervention_derives_a_marked_record, text_without_the_exact_pattern_derives_nothing, an_intervention_without_a_job_derives_nothing and a_code_outside_the_http_range_derives_nothing; all four passed when I ran them.

criteria.criterion: The backtest report lists derived records separately from observed ones, labels them derived, and cites the source intervention id. D87's firing cites the derived record and, through it, ar1x.
criteria.evidence: From reading backtest.rs: Report has `host_errors_read` and a separate `derived_host_errors: Vec<DerivedCite>`. render() prints 'host errors: N observed by the client', then a separate 'host errors derived from interventions (not observed by the client)' list, one '- derived <id> (derived, not observed; from intervention <id>)' line per record. In run_on, the under-review citations take DerivedCite::citation for derived records, and SignalRun keeps derived_records separate from host_error_records. The integration test checks that the citation names the derived record and ar1x.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets`, then `cargo fmt --check`: all pass. This includes a backtest test with a fixture intervention whose text states an HTTP 405 on a merge, showing D87 flagged under review through a derived record, and a fixture with no such text showing nothing flagged.
criteria.evidence: All three commands passed: tests ok, clippy finished with no warnings, fmt printed nothing. findings.summary: The real result (D87 flagged through ar1x) cannot be confirmed in the verifier's tree
findings.evidence: records/ is absent here, so `cargo run -p athena-cli -- backtest` read 0 interventions. Whether the real run derives a record depends on the real ar1x record having a `job` field and the text 'HTTP 405' and 'merge'. If ar1x has no job, nothing is derived and condition (b) still fails.

findings.summary: An intervention file that fails full record validation is silently skipped for derivation
findings.evidence: `if let Ok(AnyRecord::Intervention(intervention)) = AnyRecord::parse(...)` drops parse errors. Each file is still read as an InterventionRow, so a record with a validation problem would quietly derive nothing instead of being reported.

findings.summary: A derived record's id is the intervention's id, so the citation repeats the same id
findings.evidence: The citation renders as '20261013-192156-ar1x (derived, not observed; from intervention 20261013-192156-ar1x)'. The doc comment explains that the marker, not the id, tells a derived record apart, but the repeated id may confuse readers.

summary: The change does both things the request asked for. D87's intervention signal now matches class "code", and its name and the module doc say so. HostError gains a typed `derived` flag and an optional `source_intervention`. Validation rejects a derived record that has no source, and an observed record that has one. `derive_host_error` in watcher.rs uses the strict pattern: `HTTP ` plus exactly three digits from 100 to 599, the whole word merge, merges or merged, and a job on the intervention. The backtest keeps derived records in memory and never writes them under records/. Its report lists them apart from observed records and labels them "not observed by the client". When D87 is put under review, the citation names the derived record and, through it, the source intervention. I ran `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`, and all three pass. The new tests also pass: the record-validation test, four derivation unit tests (a match, a non-match, a missing job, an out-of-range code), and two backtest integration tests (an HTTP 405 on a merge puts only D87 under review through a derived record; text with no such statement flags nothing). `cargo run -p athena-cli -- backtest` runs. Here records/ is absent by design, so it read 0 interventions and derived 0 records. Both D87 signals did not fire, condition (b) is a finding, and no decision is flagged. I could not see the real records, so I cannot confirm that the real run derives a record from ar1x. That depends on the real ar1x record naming job 9h2j and containing the text 'HTTP 405' and 'merge'. Only the producer's report, which I could not see, can show it. Every changed file is on the deliverables list.
